text:
maya: FYI saw a spike of GeoDNS failovers ~18:02 UTC, some APAC nodes got SNAT exhaustion and ended up pinned to us via latency fallback. Not full outage but 5-10% of requests showed >1s egress latency :thinking:

owen: ugh. which fallback policy fired? latency-based or region-pin?

sara: looks like latency-based with 'closest healthy' rolled forward. A few backends reported `conn reset` and we exhausted SNAT on the egress NAT gateway.

kyle: can you paste the health check logs? also which LB flavor, NLB or ALB?

maya: LB = NLB in front of the GPU pool in apac-south. Health checks: `502` spikes then most traffic rerouted. snippet from probe logs:
```
2027-06-01T18:01:44Z probe check -> 200
2027-06-01T18:02:03Z probe check -> 502 (upstream reset)
2027-06-01T18:02:05Z probe check -> 502
2027-06-01T18:02:10Z probe check -> 502
```

james-oncall: infra-bot reported SNAT usage high on gateway gw-apac-01 at 18:02:08, then GeoDNS moved ~12% traffic to us-east-1 as fallback.

infra-bot: [alert] snat-utilization gw-apac-01=0.98 threshold=0.9 -> action=notify

owen: that explains the latency bump. If GeoDNS decides nearest healthy and APAC is unhealthy, traffic will route farther -> latency. We should avoid blowing SNAT capacity when failover happens (cascade).

sara: two quick mitigations: 1) increase SNAT ports (short-term, costs money), 2) adjust GeoDNS fallback policy to prefer regional pinning for GPU-heavy routes so we don't cross continents for sudden small failures.

kyle: agree on regional pinning, but we need a circuit-breaker so single-region SNAT exhaustion doesn't fail the whole region. Proposal draft below:
```yaml
fallback_policy:
  type: prioritized_regions
  prefer_pin: true
  allowed_fallbacks:
    - same_region
    - same_continent
    - global
circuit_breaker:
  snat_threshold: 0.85
  action: throttle_fallbacks
  cooldown: 120s
```

maya: i like throttle_fallbacks — basically limit how much traffic GeoDNS can shove out-of-region during a sharp SNAT spike.

james-oncall: how would throttle_fallbacks interact with canary rollouts? we run canaries to new GPU versions in eu-west and sometimes use cross-region bursts.

sara: canary traffic should be tagged and excluded from throttle OR assigned different priority so we don't penalize releases. We'll mark canary routes with header `x-rw-canary: true`.

owen: operational checklist to ship this safely:
- add snat_threshold metric and dashboards (1m, 5m)
- implement `throttle_fallbacks` in geo router (rate-limit trail reroutes per region)
- add canary tag exclusion
- run chaos test (fail gateway) in staging for 30m and validate no cross-continent explosion

kyle: estimates: dashboard + metric ~2d, geo router change ~3d, tests + runbook ~1d. Config rollout as A/B then global.

maya: cost note: increasing SNAT capacity across apac pools is ~+$1.6k/month, but cross-region egress increase from routing to us-east could be ~$8k/mo depending on token traffic. Pinning + throttle likely cheaper.

sara: flagging this to product: edge-cost alert. product@redwood: if we pin stricter, some customers in APAC might see brief reduced quality when local infra is unhealthy. Tradeoff decision.

james-oncall: i'll open an incident-style postmortem doc but marking low sev for now; will run a dry-run of the throttle rule in simulation first.

maya: OK, next actions: @owen please add metric + grafana panel, @kyle start geo-router PR draft, @sara draft runbook & canary exclusion. i'll ping legal/product re: customer impact.

owen: on it. starting panels now.

kyle: starting PR in eng-infra repo -> will link when ready.

sara: runbook skeleton in #eng-oncall, will invite @james-oncall to review.

maya: thanks team. we'll reconvene after the simulation run (ETA 36h). :thumbsup:
